info.description: REST API for Syka Remittance & Cross-Border Payment Platform
info.title: Syka Backend API

get.description: Returns issued API keys (metadata only — the secret is never returned after creation).

post.description: Issues a new API key. The full secret is returned ONCE in the response (only its hash is stored). Use it as a Bearer token for programmatic/partner access.

delete.description: Deactivates an API key so it can no longer be used.

get.description: Returns audit entries for failed login attempts (login action with a 4xx status).
Returns immutable audit-log entries with optional user/action filters, newest first.
Returns security-relevant audit entries — authentication actions that failed (4xx) — newest first.

post.description: Sends an in-app + out-of-band notification to all users matching an optional audience filter (account_type / kyc_status / country / min_tier). Records the broadcast.

get.description: Commercial channel partners — the larger institutional relationships with a revenue-share agreement, as opposed to merchants. Same filters and shape as the merchant list; they share one collection discriminated by `kind`. NOTE: this is the COMMERCIAL partner CRM. `GET /admin/partners` is a different thing entirely — the technical registry of payment providers we integrate with.

parameters.description: Match legal/trading name, code or referral code
parameters.name: search

post.description: Registers a commercial channel partner. Identical to merchant creation except the record's `kind`, which determines which admin tree can see and edit it. Starts `pending` and earns nothing until approved.

get.description: Applications currently working through onboarding for the channel-partner track, newest first, with the same stage/status/search filters as the merchant applications list. Use /admin/merchants/applications for the merchant track — both read one collection discriminated by `kind`.

parameters.description: submitted | background_check | interview | documents | approved | rejected | onboarded
parameters.name: stage

get.description: Full commercial CRM profile for a channel partner: legal entity, contacts, tier, revenue-share arrangement, scores, status history and check-ins. Returns 404 for a merchant id.
The customers attributed to this channel partner, newest first. Same data and rules as the merchant client list.
get.summary: Customers referred by a channel partner (admin)

get.description: Agreements and due-diligence files held for a channel partner, newest first. Each carries a SHORT-LIVED presigned `url` valid for 15 minutes — the storage bucket is private, so do not cache or share the link. A document whose `url` is absent could not be signed; the metadata is still returned. Returns metadata with no urls when document storage is not configured on this deployment.

post.description: Stores an agreement or due-diligence file (multipart `file`, max 10 MB). Accepts PDF, JPEG, PNG, Word and Excel only — this is an agreements store, not a general file host. Optional `name` and `doc_type` form fields label the document; `name` defaults to the filename. The file goes to private object storage and only its key is recorded, so it is always served back through a short-lived presigned link. Returns 503 when document storage is not configured.

get.description: The revenue-share position for a channel partner: earned, paid, outstanding, and the payout history. Same computation as merchant commission — a share of our platform fee on completed attributed transactions, with reversed transactions excluded.

Customer, volume and transaction trends for a channel partner. Same computation and caveats as merchant performance — `scores` are admin judgement, the rest is derived from completed attributed transactions.

put.description: Same lifecycle and rules as the merchant status change: guarded transitions, an audited reason, and commission accrual stopping the moment a partner leaves approved/active.
put.summary: Approve, suspend or terminate a channel partner (admin)

get.description: Transactions attributed to this channel partner at creation time. Same snapshot semantics as the merchant transaction list.
get.summary: Transactions attributed to a channel partner (admin)

get.description: Commission payouts across merchants and channel partners, newest first. Filter by `kind` (merchant | partner) and `status` (pending | paid | cancelled). Each row is a BATCH of accruals settled together, not one transaction's commission. Amounts are decimal strings in the settlement currency.

post.description: Generates a PDF summarising the platform-wide commission position — paid this month, pending, total outstanding, lifetime earned and the count of partners currently owed. Returns a FILE download (Content-Disposition attachment), not the JSON envelope. For a single partner's statement use POST /admin/merchants/{id}/report instead. NOTE: the PDF uses Latin-1 core fonts, so characters outside that range render as "?".

get.description: Stat-card figures for the commissions screen: paid this month, pending payouts, total outstanding, partners with unpaid commission, and lifetime commission earned. `total_outstanding` is accrued-but-unsettled commission and should match the commission-payable balance in the ledger — a persistent divergence means an accrual posted without its ledger pair and is worth investigating. Reversed accruals are excluded from every figure.

post.description: Settles a pending payout: its accruals become paid and the commission-payable liability is discharged in the ledger. IDEMPOTENT — marking an already-paid payout returns it unchanged rather than double-posting. Only a `pending` payout can be settled; anything else is 422. This RECORDS that money was sent — it does not move money, because commission is paid out of band by finance. Pass `payment_reference` to record the bank or transfer reference.

get.description: Returns compliance cases raised by the monitoring rules / watchlist, optionally filtered by status (open|dismissed|escalated|held).
Returns a single compliance case with its action history.

post.description: Records a decision on a case: dismiss, escalate, or hold. The actor and note are stored on the case timeline.

get.description: Returns the AML risk profile (LOW|MEDIUM|HIGH|VERY_HIGH) for a user, or 404 if none has been set.

put.description: Sets a manual compliance override of a user's AML risk level (LOW|MEDIUM|HIGH|VERY_HIGH). Upserts the risk profile and records the acting officer.

get.description: Returns the admin-configured transaction-monitoring rules (threshold/velocity/structuring/geo).

post.description: Creates a transaction-monitoring rule. action=hold blocks a matching send (ON_HOLD + case); action=alert only raises a case. Evaluated at send time.

put.description: Replaces a monitoring rule's parameters.

delete.description: Removes a monitoring rule.

get.description: Returns Suspicious Activity Report drafts and submissions.

post.description: Creates a Suspicious Activity Report draft.

put.description: Edits a SAR draft, or submits it when submit=true.

post.description: Screens a name/phone/email/country against the internal watchlist and returns any hits. (TransFi performs the regulated sanctions screening; this is our additional internal layer.) Every screen is recorded to the screening history and is retrievable per user via GET /admin/users/{user_id}/screening.

get.description: Returns the internal AML watchlist entries.

post.description: Adds an internal watchlist entry (kind name|phone|email|country). Matching beneficiaries are held at send time.

delete.description: Removes an internal watchlist entry.

get.description: Returns the configured send→receive corridors and the partners that service each.

post.description: Configures a send→receive corridor, its delivery methods, and the partners (priority order) that service it.

put.description: Replaces a corridor's delivery methods, partners, priority, and active flag.

delete.description: Removes a corridor configuration.

get.description: Returns the admin-managed supported-country list (send/receive flags, currency, dial code).

post.description: Creates or updates a supported country (keyed by ISO alpha-2 code), including its send/receive availability.

put.description: Updates a supported country identified by the path code.
put.summary: Update a supported country by code (admin)

delete.description: Removes a supported country by ISO alpha-2 code.

get.description: Returns all feature flags and their enabled state.

post.description: Creates a feature flag with a unique name and initial enabled state.

put.description: Replaces a feature flag's name, description, and enabled state.

delete.description: Permanently removes a feature flag.

put.description: Sets a feature flag's enabled state without other changes.

get.description: Returns all configured fee/markup rules (active and inactive), highest priority first.

post.description: Creates a fee/markup rule. Takes effect on the next quote — no deployment needed. Model is one of fx_markup, flat, percentage, tiered, combo.

put.description: Replaces a fee rule's matchers, model, and parameters. Takes effect on the next quote.

delete.description: Permanently removes a fee rule.

put.description: Activates or deactivates a fee rule without deleting it.

get.description: Returns the configured financial partners (or KYC providers), priority-ordered. These drive the routing layer (distinct from the live partner-health endpoints).

post.description: Registers a partner/provider config (name, countries, payment methods, priority, non-secret config). Secrets stay in env/Vault, not here.
post.summary: Create a financial partner / KYC provider (admin)

put.description: Replaces a partner/provider config.
put.summary: Update a financial partner / KYC provider (admin)

delete.description: Removes a partner/provider config.
delete.summary: Delete a financial partner / KYC provider (admin)

get.description: Returns the configured fee rules that use the fx_markup model (a convenience view over the fee engine).
Current per-tier daily/monthly limits (USD). Static MVP config; moves to remit_config when the limits engine lands. NOTE: these limits are display-only — nothing on the send path enforces them yet.
Returns the country→provider matrix used by the routing layer.

post.description: Maps a country to a provider (financial or kyc) with a priority.

put.description: Replaces a matrix entry.

delete.description: Removes a matrix entry.

get.description: Every role the platform defines, grouped by the app context it can log in through, with a human label, a description and the permissions that role currently holds. Use it to drive role pickers and to decide which admin controls to render. IMPORTANT: `permissions` is ADVISORY — the only authorization enforced at request time is the role allow-list on each route, so the permission list describes what the routes accept today rather than a separately enforced policy. `permission_catalogue` returns every permission code with its label so a UI can render a legend.
Returns all runtime system settings (key/value), sorted by key.

put.description: Creates or updates a batch of system settings (key/value/description). Takes effect immediately.

get.description: Returns one system setting by key.

delete.description: Removes a system setting by key.

get.description: Platform metrics: user counts (by status + KYC tier), the KYC funnel, transaction volume/value by status, fee revenue (USDC), and registered partners. Filter the transaction window with ?period=24h|7d|30d|90d|all (default 30d).

Returns KYC/KYB applications, paginated, newest first. Defaults to status=manual_review, which is what this endpoint has always returned. Pass status to reach the others: pending is the important one, because a customer registered by a merchant or a teller who is stuck at in_progress holds a pending application that never becomes manual_review, so until now they appeared in no admin queue and there was no way to find the record at all. An unrecognised status falls back to manual_review rather than returning an empty page that would read as "nothing to review". Note that approve and reject act on an application id and only make sense for an application awaiting a decision; to clear a stuck customer use POST /admin/kyc/users/{user_id}/reset, which is keyed by user.

post.description: Clears a verification that is wedged in a non-final state so the user can start again, and expires the pending application. This is the manual escape hatch: the user-facing flow already resumes an interrupted session and reconciles against the provider on its own, so reach for this only when the provider itself is stuck or reconciliation cannot resolve the state. Refuses with 422 KYC_ALREADY_APPROVED for a verified user — resetting them would silently strip their tier entitlement; use the KYC tier controls instead. The reason is recorded in the audit log.
Approves an application and sets the user's KYC tier and status accordingly.
Rejects an application and marks the user's KYC status as rejected.

get.description: Merchants in the referral network, newest first, with search/status/tier filters and pagination. `search` matches legal name, trading name, partner code or referral code. Merchants and commercial partners share one collection discriminated by `kind`, so this returns ONLY merchants — a commercial partner will not appear here and its id will 404 on these routes; use /admin/channel-partners for those.

parameters.description: Match legal/trading name, code or referral code
parameters.name: search

post.description: Registers a merchant in the referral network. `code` and `referral_code` are generated when omitted, so a merchant is always attributable — the referral code is what links a customer to them at registration. The merchant starts in `pending` status and earns NOTHING until it is moved to approved or active, so a mistyped commission rate cannot start paying out immediately. Set the commission arrangement here or later via PUT /admin/merchants/{id}/commission-rate.

409.description: Code or referral code already used

get.description: The onboarding pipeline for the merchant track, newest first. Filter by `stage` (submitted, background_check, interview, documents, approved, rejected, onboarded), by coarse `status`, or search legal/trading name and contact. Stage movement is guarded — an application cannot skip straight to approved, and rejected/onboarded are terminal.

post.description: Starts an application at the `submitted` stage with every background check pending. Creating an application does NOT create a merchant — that happens at onboarding, so an approval can still be reviewed before credentials and a live commission arrangement exist.

get.description: Counts of merchant applications broken down by stage and by status, for the pipeline stat cards. A stage with no applications is simply absent from the map rather than reported as zero, so read it defensively.
One application with its full onboarding record: background-check findings, interview checklist and notes, requested documents, and the stage history showing who moved it and when.

post.description: Marks the application approved, optionally recording the tier and commission arrangement the resulting partner should start on. This does NOT create the merchant or issue credentials — call /onboard for that. Separating the two means an approval can be reviewed before anything goes live and before any commission can accrue.

put.description: Saves due-diligence results and moves the application to `background_check`. Send only the checks you are recording — omitted fields keep their existing result, so this can be filled in over several passes. IMPORTANT: every field here is a MANUALLY RECORDED admin finding. PEP, sanctions and adverse-media are NOT automated screening — we have no screening vendor connected, so these record what a reviewer checked, not what a system verified.

get.description: The files a merchant applicant uploaded during self-registration, newest first, each with a short-lived (15 minute) presigned download link. Without this the uploads on a self-registered application cannot be reviewed at all - the partner-side document list is keyed on the partner id, which does not exist until the application is onboarded. At onboarding these same documents are re-stamped onto the new partner record, so nothing is lost or duplicated.

post.description: Records the documents asked for and moves the application to the `documents` stage, emailing the applicant. Requests are APPENDED to any earlier ones, so asking for more paperwork never erases what was already requested or received.

put.description: Records the interview and training checklist plus free-text notes, and moves the application to the `interview` stage. `conducted_at` defaults to now. The checklist is REPLACED by what you send, so submit the full list rather than a delta.

post.description: Books the interview and moves the application to the `interview` stage, emailing the applicant's contact. `scheduled_at` must be in the future. Delivery of the notification is best-effort and does not affect the booking.

Turns an approved application into a live partner. Creates the channel-partner record with a generated partner code and REFERRAL CODE, provisions a merchant-context manager login, emails a welcome message with both, and schedules a first check-in (default 30 days). Only an `approved` application can be onboarded, and only once — 422 otherwise. The response carries a ONE-TIME `temp_password` that is never retrievable again; share it securely. CAVEAT: the merchant app (/api/v1/merchant/*) is not built yet, so the manager account can authenticate but reaches no routes — the credentials exist so onboarding is real rather than a promise. If the login cannot be created (e.g. the email is already registered) the partner is still created and the response says so, so an admin can issue credentials separately.
Declines an application with a required reason and notifies the applicant. Rejection is TERMINAL — a rejected application cannot be reopened or approved later; start a new application instead.

Emails the onboarding toolkit to the applicant and stamps `toolkit_sent_at`. Deliberately does NOT move the pipeline stage — the toolkit can legitimately be sent at several points, so sending it is recorded on the history without disturbing where the application sits.

get.description: Full merchant profile: identity, contacts, status and its audit trail, tier, risk level, commission arrangement, admin-maintained scores, training record and scheduled check-ins. Returns 404 for a commercial partner id — use /admin/channel-partners/{id} for those.

Every branch belonging to one merchant, including closed ones. Branches are the merchant's own physical locations; a branch id is stamped onto every customer registered and every payment taken there, and the merchant app's branch reports are built from those snapshots. A merchant with no branches still works - its customers and payments are simply recorded without one and appear as "unattributed" in branch reports.

post.description: Creates a branch for one merchant. The code is the merchant's own label for the location and must be unique WITHIN that merchant - two different merchants may both have a branch called HQ. Branches are created here rather than by the merchant because a branch id is snapshotted onto every customer and payment, and letting a merchant invent branches freely would make their own reporting history unstable. Assign staff to a branch when provisioning their account.
post.summary: Add a branch to a merchant (admin)

put.description: Updates a branch's name, city, address, phone or open/closed state. Only fields present in the body are written. The code cannot be changed: it is the branch's stable identifier within the merchant and every export the merchant has already filed refers to it. Setting active=false closes the branch - it stops appearing in the merchant's pickers, but customers and payments already attributed to it keep that attribution, so historical branch reports do not change. A branch id belonging to a different merchant returns 404.

post.description: Records a scheduled relationship call against the merchant. `scheduled_at` must be in the future. NOTE: this RECORDS the commitment for a relationship manager to work from — nothing fires on the due date, because there is no scheduler for partner check-ins. Do not build a reminder UX expecting a notification.

get.description: The customers attributed to this merchant, newest first. Attribution is set by the merchant's referral code at registration or by an admin via PUT /admin/users/{user_id}/channel-partner. Merchant staff accounts are excluded — an employee is not a referred customer.

What this merchant has earned, been paid and is still owed, plus their payout history. Commission is a share of OUR platform fee on completed attributed transactions — never a share of the transfer amount, and never the provider's fee. `outstanding` is accrued-but-unsettled commission and matches the commission-payable balance in the ledger. Reversed transactions are excluded: their accrual is marked reversed and drops out of every figure. Amounts are decimal strings in the settlement currency.

put.description: Sets the commission arrangement. `percentage` takes a flat `rate` as a decimal FRACTION of our platform fee ("0.20" = 20% of the fee, not 20% of the transfer). `tiered` takes brackets matched on the partner's lifetime referred volume, where an omitted or "0" max_volume is the open-ended top bracket. The rate is capped at 1 (100% of our fee). IMPORTANT: this is FORWARD-LOOKING ONLY — every accrual snapshots the rate in force when it was earned, so changing the rate never rewrites past commission or an already-issued statement.

post.description: Batches every outstanding accrual for this merchant into a payout record and marks it paid, discharging the commission-payable liability in the ledger. Accruals are CLAIMED ATOMICALLY, so two admins clicking at once cannot pay the same commission twice — the second gets 422 NOTHING_TO_PAY. This records that the money was sent; it does NOT move money, because commission is settled out of band by finance. Pass `payment_reference` to record the bank/transfer reference alongside it.

Sends a message to the merchant's primary contact (falling back to the first contact with an address for the channel). Defaults to email; `sms` requires a contact phone. Delivery is BEST-EFFORT and dispatched in the background — a 200 means queued, not delivered. Returns 422 NO_CONTACT when the merchant has no address on record for the channel, and 503 when no delivery provider is configured on this deployment.

get.description: Computed activity for a merchant: total and newly-referred customers, customers active in the last 30 days, a retention rate, and a monthly acquisition/volume/fee trend. `scores` are the ADMIN-MAINTAINED judgement ratings from the merchant record, not computed — everything else is derived from completed transactions attributed to this merchant. Volume and fees are in the settlement currency.

post.description: Generates a branded PDF statement for a merchant covering their profile, commission position and recent payouts. Returns a FILE download (Content-Disposition attachment), not the JSON envelope, so do not parse it as JSON. NOTE: the PDF uses Latin-1 core fonts, so characters outside that range in a legal name render as "?".

Creates an additional login for one of a merchant's people and returns a temporary password that is shown ONCE. Set manager=true for MERCHANT_MANAGER, which additionally allows deciding payment approvals, blocking customers, setting their limits and comparing branches; otherwise the account is MERCHANT_STAFF. Assigning branch_id is what makes a branch more than a label: it is copied onto every customer that person registers and every payment they take, and the merchant's branch reports are built from those snapshots. A branch id belonging to a different merchant returns 404. Onboarding creates only the first manager, before any branch exists - everyone after that is created here.

put.description: Moves a merchant through its lifecycle, recording who changed it and why on an immutable status history. Legal moves: pending→approved/terminated, approved→active/suspended/terminated, active→suspended/terminated, suspended→active/terminated. Anything else is 422 INVALID_STATE_TRANSITION; terminated is final. IMPORTANT: a merchant only EARNS commission while approved or active — suspending stops accrual on the next transaction immediately, though commission already earned is untouched and still payable. Terminating also deactivates the record.
put.summary: Approve, suspend or terminate a merchant (admin)

put.description: Moves a merchant between bronze, silver, gold and platinum. Tier is a commercial label used for reporting and banding; it does NOT itself change what the merchant earns — commission comes from the arrangement set on /commission-rate. Change both if the tier is meant to carry a different rate.
put.summary: Upgrade or downgrade a merchant tier (admin)

get.description: Training modules, certifications and any expiry alerts for a merchant. This is REFERENCE DATA maintained by admins — nothing here is delivered or assessed by the platform, and no module is automatically marked complete. `alerts` lists certifications and modules that have expired or expire within 30 days.

Transactions whose sender was attributed to this merchant WHEN THE TRANSFER WAS CREATED. Attribution is snapshotted onto each transaction, not looked up live, so reassigning a customer never changes which merchant a past transfer counted for. Equivalent to GET /admin/transactions?channel_partner_id=. Optional status filter.

Returns the SIGNED-IN admin's own event-alert settings: `channels` (the shared in-app/email/SMS/push toggles), `alerts` (per-alert-type in-app/email settings, defaults merged under any saved values so the object is always fully populated), and `catalogue` (every alert type with its label, description, whether it takes a threshold, and its default) so the UI renders toggles from the API instead of hardcoding them. These are per-admin and self-scoped — there is no endpoint to read another admin's preferences. IMPORTANT: nothing consumes these toggles yet; no alert emitters exist, so changing one has no delivery effect today.

put.description: Patches the signed-in admin's own alert settings. PARTIAL by design — send only what changed. Omitted channels and omitted alert types are left untouched, and within an alert type an omitted field is untouched, so two admins editing different alerts cannot clobber each other and an older client cannot wipe an alert type it does not know about. `threshold_usd` is a decimal STRING and is only accepted on alert types whose catalogue entry has `supports_threshold: true`. An unknown alert code is a 400 rather than a silently ignored setting. Returns the full merged preferences.

get.description: Returns admin-managed notification templates (email/sms/in-app).

post.description: Creates an admin-managed notification template.

put.description: Replaces a notification template.

delete.description: Removes a notification template.

get.description: Returns all physical offices.

post.description: Creates a physical office (unique code).

put.description: Replaces an office's details.

delete.description: Removes an office.

post.description: Assigns a teller account to this office (sets office_id on the teller).
post.summary: Assign a teller to an office (admin)

get.description: Returns the staff assigned to one office - tellers and supervisors, with their role and account status. Nothing else ever answered "who works at this branch": assignment was writable through POST /admin/offices/{id}/assign-teller but not readable back, so there was no way to confirm it had worked or to see a branch roster. Identity and status only, deliberately - this is a staffing view, not a user record, so it carries no KYC, address or verification data. Capped at 200; an office with more staff than that needs a paged endpoint, which nothing has asked for.
get.summary: List the tellers assigned to an office

get.description: Returns the registered financial partners and the corridors each declares it supports.
Pings every registered partner with a lightweight read and reports up/degraded/down with latency. Use for the partner monitoring dashboard.

post.description: Runs a live connectivity test against a single registered partner by name.

get.description: Returns previously requested async report jobs (without the file payload), newest first.

post.description: Queues a report for asynchronous generation by the worker (use for large exports). Returns the job; poll GET /admin/reports/{id} and download via GET /admin/reports/{id}/download when ready.

get.description: Generates and streams a report synchronously as CSV (default), XLSX (?format=xlsx) or PDF (?format=pdf). Filter with ?from=&to= (RFC3339 or YYYY-MM-DD) and ?status=. Report kinds: transactions, users, revenue, kyc, partner-settlement. PDF is for printing and sign-off, not bulk data: a report over 5,000 rows returns 422 REPORT_TOO_LARGE_FOR_PDF and should be requested as XLSX instead. PDF also uses Latin-1 core fonts, so characters outside that range render as "?".
Returns an async report job's status and metadata.
Streams the file for a ready async report job. Returns 422 if the job is not yet ready.

Revenue and settled volume grouped by the RECIPIENT's country, highest revenue first, capped at 100 rows. Onramp and offramp transactions have no recipient country and are grouped under `UNKNOWN` rather than being dropped, so the rows still reconcile to the summary total.

Revenue and settled volume grouped by the financial partner that settled each transfer. NOTE: all traffic currently routes through a single partner, so expect exactly one row — the endpoint is shaped as a breakdown so the view need not change when multi-partner routing lands.

Splits revenue by HOW it was charged, using the fee engine's own `fee_mode`: `transaction_fees` is the fee the sender saw itemised, `fx_spread` is the markup folded into the quoted rate. `partner_fees` is flagged `is_cost: true` — it is the provider's charge to us and is subtracted from gross to give net, so a UI must not sum it with the others. `treasury_management` is always zero and reported for completeness: Syka holds no customer balances, so there is no treasury product to earn on.

parameters.description: Start date (YYYY-MM-DD or RFC3339); overrides period
parameters.name: from

parameters.description: End date (YYYY-MM-DD or RFC3339); overrides period
parameters.name: to

get.description: Headline revenue for today, this week, this month and all time, side by side for the dashboard stat row. `gross_revenue` is OUR platform fee (the explicit fee plus any FX markup) in the settlement currency; `provider_cost` is what the payment provider charges us and is SUBTRACTED to give `net_revenue` — never render it as income. Only COMPLETED transactions count, so a failed or pending transfer never inflates the figure. All amounts are decimal strings in USDC because that is the only currency every transaction shares.

Senders ranked by the revenue they generated in the window, with lifetime volume, average fee per transaction and transaction count. Names and emails are joined from the user record; a sender whose account has since been removed shows as "(unknown)" rather than being dropped from the ranking.

Revenue as a dated time series for charting, bucketed by day (default), week or month. Each point carries gross revenue, provider cost, net revenue, settled volume and transaction count. Buckets with no completed transactions are omitted rather than emitted as zero — plot against the returned dates rather than assuming a contiguous range.

Cross-entity search for the admin top-nav box. Matches users (email, phone, first/last name), transactions (exact reference then reference prefix), beneficiaries (name, nickname) and compliance cases (case id, transaction reference, user id). Query must be at least 2 characters; `limit` is per section (default 5, max 20). Sections run concurrently under a 3s budget each: a section that fails or times out returns an empty array AND is named in `sections_failed`, so an empty list there does not mean "no matches". `sections_omitted` names sections the caller's role may not see — compliance cases are hidden from SUPPORT_AGENT and FINANCE_ADMIN. NOTE: beneficiary bank details are NOT searchable by design — payout details are stored encrypted, so an account number cannot be matched.

Returns all transactions across users with optional status/type/sender/teller filters, paginated. `teller_id` scopes to the transactions a given teller processed (teller-assisted sends only, since only those carry a teller).

parameters.description: Filter by the teller who processed the transaction
parameters.name: teller_id

parameters.description: Filter by the merchant/channel partner the sender was attributed to
parameters.name: channel_partner_id

get.description: Returns full detail for any transaction by reference (not owner-scoped).

post.description: Moves a non-terminal transaction to ON_HOLD for compliance review.

Releases an ON_HOLD transaction. For a remittance held by the compliance hook before any funds were collected, this creates the collection order and returns the transaction to PENDING with a fresh `checkout_url` for the sender; otherwise it restores the status implied by how far the transfer had already got. Safe to retry: a release that failed at the payment provider can be attempted again, and a transaction that is already resumed is left alone.
Returns 422 CANNOT_RESUME when the transfer cannot be restarted — the sender is no longer eligible (account or verification status), or the transfer predates the `send_payment_type` requirement and has no payment method stored, in which case the sender must start a new transfer.

Reverses a COMPLETED transaction on our books — posts compensating double-entry ledger entries and sets the status to REVERSED. NOTE: TransFi has no programmatic refund, so the actual return of funds is a TransFi-support action; the reason is recorded for follow-up. Idempotent.

422.description: Only a COMPLETED transaction can be reversed

get.description: Returns our provider MCA / prefunding balances (available prefunding, collections, payouts, unsettled) per currency. Use it to confirm a prefund landed and how much float is available to cover payouts. Optionally filter with ?currency=USDC.

post.description: Tops up our provider prefunding (MCA) balance — the pool that payouts draw from — via a fiat_prefund (fiat funding → stablecoin float). source_currency defaults to USD (payment_code ach), dest_currency to USDC; source_details supplies the funding account's email + bank fields. Sends a 6-digit reset OTP to the account's registered phone or email.

Verifies a 2FA code to finalise a login that returned requires_2fa: true. The temp_token expires in 5 minutes.
method values: "totp" — 6-digit code from an authenticator app (Google Authenticator, Authy, etc.); "sms" — 6-digit code sent to the registered phone; "backup_code" — one of the 8 single-use codes shown at 2FA setup time.

Exchanges a refresh token for a new access + refresh token pair (automatic rotation).
Access tokens expire after 15 minutes. Call this endpoint when a request returns 401 to get a new pair without re-login.
The old refresh token is invalidated immediately — always save both new tokens to local storage before discarding the old ones.
Refresh tokens last 30 days. If a refresh token is used twice (replay attack), the entire token family is revoked and the user must log in again (401 TOKEN_FAMILY_REVOKED).
EXCEPTION: a token sent again within 10 seconds of being exchanged (or by two requests at once) is treated as a client race, not theft: 409 REFRESH_TOKEN_RACE, nothing issued and nothing revoked. On 409, do NOT refresh again and do NOT log the user out - re-read the tokens the successful refresh just stored and retry the original request with them. Make refresh single-flight: one in-flight refresh at a time, and persist the new refresh token before any other request is sent.

401.description: Token invalid, expired, already used, or account deactivated

409.description: REFRESH_TOKEN_RACE: token already exchanged moments ago; retry with the stored new tokens

Sets whether the account is personal or business. account_type accepted values: "individual" or "corporate".

post.description:
Activates the account, provisions an internal accounting wallet, issues a full access + refresh token pair, and silently registers the user with our financial partner (TransFi).
All previous steps (verify-otp, set-password, personal-info, account-type) must be completed first or a 422 is returned.
The wallet created here is an internal ledger balance — it is not a blockchain wallet and does not hold actual funds. A blockchain payment rail is used transparently when the user initiates a transaction.
The financial partner registration (TransFi) happens in the background and is completely transparent to the frontend — no extra step is required. If the partner registration fails (e.g. partner API is down), the user account is still activated; the registration is retried separately.
On success, store both access_token and refresh_token. The access token expires in 15 minutes; the refresh token lasts 30 days.

Validates the phone number, creates a pending account, and sends a 6-digit OTP via SMS.
Phone formats accepted: E.164 ("+233542848250") or local format ("0542848250") with a 2-letter ISO country_code ("GH"). The number is always stored as E.164 internally.
app_context must be "user" — tellers and admins cannot self-register; they are provisioned by staff.
The registration_token in the response must be passed to every subsequent registration step. It is valid for 30 minutes.
If the phone already has a pending (incomplete) registration, a new OTP is sent and the same flow continues.

Stores the account holder's name, date of birth, and gender.
This step is required for ALL account types (individual and corporate). For corporate accounts these details represent the person opening the account, not the company.

gender accepted values: "male", "female", "other", "prefer_not_to_say".
email is REQUIRED (used to register the user with our payment partner) and must be unique. An email-verification OTP is issued; in non-production environments it is returned in dev_otp and written to the server logs.
On success, next_step is "verify_email".

The two directions serve the two halves of a transfer. `direction=withdraw` (currency = receive currency) is how the RECIPIENT is paid — it feeds `beneficiary.payment_code`/`payment_type` and `payout_details`. `direction=deposit` (currency = send currency) is how the SENDER pays — it feeds the `send_payment_code`/`send_payment_type` that POST /transactions/send requires. get.description: Returns the invoices YOU issued, newest first. Another user's invoices are never visible - every read is keyed on the issuer. Filter with ?status=active|paid|void|overdue. NOTE on overdue: it is DERIVED, not stored - an invoice reads overdue when it is still active and past its due_date, so the status field can differ from what is in the database and an invoice with no due_date is never overdue. Each row carries total (amount x max_qty) so clients do not each multiply decimal strings and round differently.

post.description: Creates an invoice for a customer you name. account_name is free text on purpose - an invoice is often raised against somebody with no Syka account, and requiring one would make the register useless for exactly those customers. amount is the UNIT price and MUST be sent as a decimal STRING ("1200.80"), never a JSON number: money is never represented as a float here. min_qty and max_qty bound how many units may be paid for and both default to 1; max_qty below min_qty is a 400. due_date is optional YYYY-MM-DD and an invoice without one is never overdue; with one, it becomes overdue at the END of that day, not the start. The invoice is created active and is not shareable until you call POST /invoices/{id}/share.

400.description: Invalid amount, quantities or due date

get.description: Resolves an invoice from a share token so a recipient can see what they are being asked to pay: who issued it, for what, how much, and whether it is still outstanding. Requires a signed-in Syka user - the payment provider only collects from a registered, verified account, so there is no anonymous checkout. This is the ONE invoice read not scoped to the issuer, which is the whole purpose of the token; it is safe because the token is unguessable, is the only way in, and is never returned by any other endpoint. The token is not echoed back in the response. `payable` says whether POST /invoices/shared/{token}/pay will work and `not_payable_reason` says why not when it is false - already paid, withdrawn, somebody else already paying it, or the issuer never nominated a payout rail. `payment_label` names the rail the money will go to (for example "mtn (local_wallet), GH") WITHOUT revealing the issuer''"'"'s account number: holding the share token must not expose their bank details, so the payer clicks pay and the server builds the transfer.

post.description: Pays somebody else's invoice from its share link, as an ordinary transfer to the rail the issuer nominated. Requires `Idempotency-Key` and the `quote_id` from POST /invoices/shared/{token}/quote. You must be signed in. THE MONEY DOES NOT LAND IN A SYKA BALANCE - it is sent to the issuer's own mobile money or bank account, exactly like any other transfer, because Syka holds no customer funds and every wallet balance is permanently zero. The response is the ordinary transaction, including `checkout_url` where the provider collects from you. THE FIRST PAYER CLAIMS THE INVOICE: a second person opening the same link gets 409 INVOICE_ALREADY_CLAIMED, so one bill cannot be paid twice. A payment that fails before reaching the provider releases the claim, so a genuine retry is never blocked. The invoice reads `paid` only when the transfer COMPLETES, not when you start it - an abandoned checkout is not a payment - and it then carries `payment_ref`, which is what distinguishes a payment we can verify from one the issuer simply recorded with mark-paid.

409.description: Already claimed, or a replayed idempotency key

422.description: Not payable, or the quote expired

post.description: Prices paying somebody else's invoice from its share link. You must be SIGNED IN - there is no anonymous checkout anywhere on this platform, because the payment provider only ever collects from a registered, verified account. The quote is priced RECEIVE-ANCHORED, so the issuer receives exactly the invoice amount and you pay that plus the fee; the quote is valid for 90 seconds and its `quote_id` is what POST /invoices/shared/{token}/pay takes. `send_payment_type` is how YOU fund it - your own deposit rail from GET /config/payment-methods?direction=deposit&currency=<your currency> - and is required for the same reason the ordinary send requires it. `quantity` defaults to the invoice's min_qty and must fall within min_qty..max_qty. Returns 422 INVOICE_NOT_PAYABLE if the issuer has not set up a way to be paid through Syka, if the invoice is already paid or withdrawn, or 409 INVOICE_ALREADY_CLAIMED if somebody else is already paying it.
post.summary: Price a payment against a shared invoice

409.description: Somebody else is already paying it

get.description: Full detail for an invoice YOU issued, including the derived status, the total, and the share path once one has been minted. An invoice belonging to another user returns 404, not 403, so invoice ids cannot be probed - and a malformed id returns 404 for the same reason, because distinguishing the two would tell a caller which ids exist.

put.description: Changes an invoice that is still active. Every field is optional and omitted fields are left alone. A PAID invoice is refused with 422 INVOICE_PAID - it is the record of a payment that happened and is not rewritten - and a withdrawn one with 422 INVOICE_VOID. amount stays a decimal STRING and must be positive; quantities are re-validated against each other, so raising min_qty above the existing max_qty is a 400 rather than a silently unpayable invoice.

delete.description: Withdraws an unpaid invoice. It is a STATUS CHANGE, not a delete: a link you already shared then resolves to a withdrawn invoice rather than a 404 a recipient would read as a broken link, and you keep the record of having raised it. A paid invoice is refused with 422 INVOICE_PAID. Withdrawing an already-withdrawn invoice succeeds and changes nothing.

post.description: Creates a NEW active invoice with the same customer, description, amount, currency and quantities. Deliberately does NOT copy the share link, the paid state or the due date: the copy is a new invoice that happens to have the same contents, and inheriting the original's link would let one payment appear to settle two. Works from a paid or withdrawn invoice too - copying the contents of a finished invoice is the common case for a repeat customer.

Marks YOUR invoice paid when the customer paid you by some other route - cash, a bank transfer, anything that did not pass through Syka. The optional note records how. An invoice settled this way has NO payment_ref, and one paid through Syka does: the two are deliberately distinguishable, because a Syka payment is verifiable and this is your own word for it. Idempotent - marking an already-paid invoice paid succeeds and changes nothing. A withdrawn invoice is refused with 422 INVOICE_VOID.
post.summary: Record a payment made outside Syka

post.description: Mints an unguessable share token and returns share_url_path, the path a recipient opens (GET /invoices/shared/{token}). A PATH rather than an absolute URL, because the API is reached on a different host per environment and the server cannot reliably know which one you came through - prefix it with your own base URL. Calling it again returns the SAME token, so a link you already sent keeps working. The token is separate from the invoice id on purpose: sharing one invoice must not expose an id space somebody could walk. A withdrawn invoice cannot be shared (422 INVOICE_VOID). IMPORTANT: the recipient must be a signed-in Syka user - the payment provider only collects from a registered, verified account, so there is no link a stranger can pay.
