post.description: Re-initiates identity (or business) verification after a rejection, reusing the type and level of the most recent application. Returns a fresh verify_url. Only valid when kyc_status is "rejected".

get.description: Returns the authenticated user's current KYC tier, verification status, and recommended next action. Poll this after opening the verify_url to detect when TransFi has processed the result.

post.description: Starts a Tier 1 identity verification for an individual user. Returns a verify_url hosted by Sumsub (via TransFi). Open this URL in a WebView or browser — the user submits their government ID and a selfie. TransFi fires a webhook when complete; poll GET /kyc/status to detect the result. Individual users only — corporate accounts use /kyb/standard/initiate. The first initiation registers the user with the payment provider, which refuses a name containing digits or symbols: that is 422 `NAME_NOT_ACCEPTED` with `details.field` (`first_name` | `last_name`) naming what to correct via PUT /users/me/profile (previously this surfaced as a bare 400 "Invalid request parameters.").

422.description: Account not yet registered with payment partner | NAME_NOT_ACCEPTED | PROFILE_INCOMPLETE

post.description: Starts a Tier 2 enhanced identity verification. Requires the user to have completed Tier 1 first (kyc_tier >= 1). Returns a verify_url for an enhanced Sumsub check. Individual users only.

422.description: Account not yet registered with payment partner

post.description: Starts Tier 3 enhanced due diligence (proof of address + source of funds) for an individual. Runs the advanced Sumsub flow via TransFi; the requested tier is recorded so approval upgrades the user to Tier 3. Individual users only.

Starts Tier 4 full enhanced due diligence (high-value / PEP, manual compliance review). Runs the advanced provider flow; final approval and limits are set by a compliance officer. Individual users only.

Step 1 of the public merchant registration wizard. Creates a DRAFT application and returns a `tracking_token` - an unguessable handle that addresses this application for an applicant who has no Syka account. There is no password and no account: keep the token, or use the recovery endpoints to have it re-sent. The token is also emailed as part of `status_url_path`. A draft is NOT visible to administrators until it is submitted, so an abandoned form never reaches the review queue. Returns 409 APPLICATION_EXISTS when an application for that email is already in progress (a rejected one does not block a new attempt). Rate limited per IP.

409.description: An application for this email is already in progress

post.description: Emails a six-digit code to the contact address on a live application, valid for ten minutes. Exchange it at /merchant-applications/recover/verify for the tracking token. ALWAYS returns 202 with the same body whether or not an application exists for that address - so this endpoint cannot be used to discover which businesses have applied. Rate limited per IP.

503.description: Recovery not available on this deployment

post.description: Exchanges the emailed six-digit code for the application's tracking token, so the applicant can continue where they left off. The code is single-use and expires after ten minutes; an invalid or expired one returns 400 INVALID_CODE. Tightly rate limited - this is the only endpoint that hands out a tracking token.
post.summary: Verify a merchant application recovery code (public)

get.description: The reference data the public merchant registration form is built from: the documents that must be uploaded (with their codes, accepted content types and size cap), the business-type choices and the target-audience choices. Unauthenticated. Render the form from this rather than hardcoding the lists - the SAME document list decides whether an application may be submitted, so a hardcoded copy would go out of step with the rule the moment compliance asks for another document. The `code` of each document is what you send as `document_type` when uploading.

The applicant's view of their own application, addressed by the tracking token: their submitted details, which required documents are still missing, whether it can be submitted yet, and where the decision stands. Unauthenticated - the token is the credential, so treat it as one. Serves both the remaining wizard steps and the post-submission status page. `status_label` is a plain-English summary; the internal review stages (background check, interview) are deliberately collapsed into "Under review". Uploaded documents are listed by name and type only, with NO download links.

put.description: Replaces the details on a DRAFT application - the wizard's Back button. Send the whole form, as on create. Returns 422 APPLICATION_SUBMITTED once it has been submitted, because a reviewer may already be working from it; corrections after that go through support. Changing the contact email to one that already has an application in progress returns 409.

post.description: Step 2 of the wizard. Multipart: `file` plus `document_type`, whose value must be one of the `code`s from GET /merchant-applications/requirements - an unrecognised code is refused rather than filed as "other", because the reviewer's checklist is built from those codes and a mislabelled upload reads as a missing one. PDF, JPEG, PNG or WebP, 10 MB maximum. Uploading the same type again REPLACES the previous file, which is how a blurred photo is corrected. Returns the full application status so the progress bar can be redrawn from one response.

400.description: Unknown document type, unsupported file type, or too large

post.description: Step 3 of the wizard. Moves the draft into the administrators' review queue, after which it can no longer be edited. Returns 422 MISSING_DOCUMENTS, naming each one in `details.missing_documents`, if any required document has not been uploaded - check `can_submit` on the status response before enabling the button. Approval happens in the Syka admin app; the applicant watches progress on the status endpoint.

get.description: Payments from the caller's own merchant that are waiting on, or have received, a manager's decision, with counts for every status so the queue tabs need no extra call. Filter by status (pending, info_requested, approved, rejected, expired) and by branch. pending and info_requested are both OPEN states - asking the submitting staff member a question decides nothing, so an approval can still be approved after a question was asked. Counts and rows are always scoped to the caller's own merchant, and a branch id from another merchant returns 404.

parameters.description: pending, info_requested, approved, rejected or expired
parameters.name: status

get.description: Full detail for one queued payment: the customer, the submitting staff member, the amounts, the threshold that triggered the approval as it stood when the payment was submitted, any messages exchanged, and the live transaction. Two fields matter for what a decision will actually do. blocked_by lists gates other than this approval that are still holding the payment - if it contains "compliance", approving will record the decision but the payment stays on hold until Syka's compliance review clears it, so the button will appear to do nothing. stale reports that the payment's locked exchange rate has aged past the merchant's approval window, in which case approving is refused and the staff member must submit the payment again at the current rate.

post.description: Approves a queued payment. ALWAYS read the action field - only "approved" means the payment is moving. Approving RE-PRICES the payment at the live rate first, because a payment released at the price it was quoted at hours ago commits us to a rate the provider will no longer transact at. If the new figures move more than the merchant's tolerance (0.5% by default, on whichever side actually moved), the response is 200 with action "requote_confirmation_required" and carries the old and new figures plus a quote id - show them to the manager and call again with accept_quote_id to release at exactly those figures. The quote expires in 90 seconds; if it does, re-approve and you will get fresh figures, which is correct because the price genuinely moved again. Within tolerance the payment is approved straight through with no second call. The merchant's own gates are re-run against the RE-PRICED amount, so approving can return 422 AMOUNT_BLOCKED or 422 LIMIT_EXCEEDED even though submission did not, and action "security_check_required" when re-pricing newly crosses the security threshold - the original security check was bound to the original quote and cannot cover a larger amount. Manager-only. Two managers deciding at once is safe: one wins, the other gets 409 ALREADY_DECIDED. Returns 422 APPROVAL_EXPIRED (replacing the old QUOTE_TOO_STALE) when the payment has waited longer than the merchant's approval window - re-pricing makes the price honest but cannot make a week-old instruction current. If Syka compliance is also holding the payment the decision is recorded but the payment stays on hold - check blocked_by on the approval detail. If creating the checkout fails the approval returns to the queue rather than being left marked approved beside a payment that never moved.

Rejects a queued payment; manager-only, and a reason of at least five characters is required because the submitting staff member has to explain the outcome to the customer. The payment is CANCELLED rather than marked failed - no money was ever collected, and cancelling returns the amount to the customer's available limit headroom, which a payment left pending would consume forever. A payment the provider has already accepted cannot be rejected here and returns 422; contact Syka support to reverse it. Two managers deciding at once is safe: one wins, the other gets 409.

Adds a message to a queued payment and notifies the staff member who submitted it; manager-only. This DECIDES NOTHING - the payment stays queued, the approval stays open, and it can still be approved or rejected afterwards, so a manager who asks a question and gets a satisfactory answer does not have to make the staff member start over. Messages are append-only and each records who wrote it and when.
post.summary: Ask the submitter for more information

get.description: Returns every branch belonging to the authenticated staff member's own merchant, each with the number of staff assigned to it. Branches are created by a Syka administrator via /admin/merchants/{id}/branches; a merchant that has none yet gets an empty list, and its customers and payments are simply recorded without a branch. Inactive branches are excluded unless include_inactive=true, so a closed branch stops appearing in pickers while its historical transactions keep their branch attribution.

Paginated directory of the customers belonging to the authenticated staff member's own merchant, never any other merchant's. Search q matches phone, email, first name and last name; status and type filter on the account record; branch_id narrows to one branch and returns 404 if the branch belongs to another merchant. NOTE on risk: risk ratings live in a separate compliance database and cannot be joined in the query, so ?risk= filters the returned page in memory and the pagination total still counts the unfiltered set - use it to skim, not to count.

post.description: Registers an individual OR a business customer for the caller's own merchant in one submission. customer_type selects the shape and is OPTIONAL: it defaults to "corporate", so callers written against the earlier business-only contract keep working unchanged. A "corporate" body needs business, registered_address, contact, directors (at least one), ubos (at least one) and compliance; an "individual" body needs individual (country_code and dob, both required because the payment provider will not verify a person without them), registered_address (their RESIDENTIAL address), contact and compliance. Sending a block that belongs to the other type - directors on an individual, say - is a 400 naming the conflicting field, never a silently ignored field. The response carries a temporary password shown ONCE and never again, and files the verification state under kyb for a business or kyc for a person. Unless start_verification (or its older alias start_kyb) is false, a verification session opens and its URL is returned. A corporate customer whose provider registration failed reads kyb.status blocked_provider_registration and cannot transact until it is retried; that state does not apply to individuals, whose provider account is created when verification starts. The profile write is fatal - a failure there removes the record rather than leaving a customer who can never be verified - while everything after it (directors, owners, wallet, verification) is reported in warnings rather than discarding the temporary password.

get.description: Downloads the merchant's own customer directory as a spreadsheet, honouring the same status, type and branch_id filters as the list endpoint. Formats are csv (default) and xlsx; PDF is deliberately not offered because the PDF renderer is capped at 5,000 rows and its built-in fonts cannot render non-Latin names. Exports are capped at 100,000 customers and a larger request is refused outright rather than silently truncated, so a file can never look complete when it is not.

Full record for one of the merchant's own customers: identity, account and KYC status, risk level, the merchant-set transaction limits, any merchant block, and a rollup of the payments this merchant has processed for them. Corporate customers also carry a kyb block whose status is blocked_provider_registration when the customer was never registered with the payment provider - that customer cannot be verified or transact until registration is retried. A customer belonging to another merchant returns 404, not 403, so customer ids cannot be probed.

put.description: Updates contact details, branch assignment and, for corporate customers, the business record of one of the merchant's own customers. Only fields present in the body are written. Changing the email address clears its verified flag, because the previous verification was of a different mailbox. Restricted to customers this merchant registered - a customer who signed up themselves owns their own record and gets 403 CUSTOMER_NOT_EDITABLE, so an agent cannot rewrite a self-service user's identity. Email and phone remain unique platform-wide, so a collision is 409.

get.description: Merged, newest-first timeline of this merchant's payments for the customer and this merchant's own staff notes about them. It deliberately does not include the customer's in-app notifications or another merchant's transactions: the timeline shows what this merchant did, not everything that ever happened to the customer.

post.description: Toggles a merchant-scoped block on one of the merchant's own customers; manager-only. A reason of at least five characters is required in both directions. This is NOT a platform suspension - it stops this merchant serving the customer and nothing else, so the customer keeps access to the mobile app, to any other merchant, and to money they already hold. A platform-wide suspension is a Syka decision made by an administrator. Send blocked=false to lift the block; the block record is cleared entirely rather than left in place with a stale reason.

get.description: Documents THIS MERCHANT holds about one of its own customers - certificates of incorporation, director identification, signed mandates - each with a download link valid for 15 minutes. These are the merchant's own uploaded copies. They are NOT the customer's verification documents: those are submitted directly to the identity provider through a hosted flow and Syka never receives them, so there is nothing to retrieve from the provider here. When document storage is not configured the metadata is still returned and the url is absent.

post.description: Stores a document against one of the merchant's own customers as multipart/form-data. Accepts PDF, JPEG, PNG, WebP, Word and Excel files up to 10 MB; the size is enforced while reading rather than trusted from the request header. Optional form fields name and doc_type label the file, defaulting to the filename and "other". Files are stored privately and are only ever served through short-lived signed links - the storage path is never returned. Uploading here does not submit anything to the identity provider: the customer's own verification happens through the provider's hosted flow.

get.description: Redirects to a signed download link for one of the merchant's own customer documents, valid for 15 minutes. The document is looked up by BOTH the customer and the merchant, so a document id from another customer or another merchant returns 404 rather than a file. The redirect points at private object storage; the link expires, so it should be followed immediately rather than stored or shared.

302.description: Redirect to the signed download URL

post.description: Sends a verification reminder by email and SMS to one of the merchant's own customers. Include customer_ids in the body to send to several at once (up to 200) - the customer in the path is used when the list is omitted. Customers whose verification is already approved are skipped rather than messaged, and ids that do not belong to this merchant are reported as skipped exactly like unknown ones, so a bulk call cannot be used to discover another merchant's customers. The response reports counts and a per-customer explanation for anything not sent.

parameters.description: Additional recipients and an optional message
parameters.name: request

post.description: Issues a hosted verification link for one of the merchant's own individual customers, and is the supported way to get a customer a fresh link after they lost or never opened the first one. It does NOT always create a new provider session: when an unfinished session is still live it returns that same URL with resumed:true, and when the local status is stale it reconciles against the provider first, so repeatedly pressing this cannot strand a customer. Hand verify_url to the customer. NOTE that this is one of TWO separate verifications - the payment provider also emails the customer its own contact-verification link, valid for only ten minutes, which we can neither resend nor bypass; GET /merchant/customers/{id}/kyc/status reports where that one stands. Business customers are refused with USE_KYB_FLOW: business verification is a different provider flow and starts at registration. A customer belonging to another merchant returns 404, not 403.
post.summary: Start or resume a customer's verification

get.description: Reads one of the merchant's own customers' verification state, asking the payment provider first rather than reporting whatever was last stored. That matters because a merchant-registered customer is otherwise never polled - the only other poller runs when the customer opens the Syka consumer app, which a walk-in never does - so a completed verification could sit at the provider indefinitely while this said in_progress. Returns the current tier and status, a resume_url when an unfinished session can still be continued, can_retry, and contact_verification: the provider's OWN email/phone check, which is separate from the Syka verification the customer completed at registration and blocks transfers until one channel is satisfied. A contact_verification status of "initiated" with an old timestamp means the provider emailed the customer a link and nobody opened it within its ten-minute life. Throttled to one provider call per customer per 20 seconds, so polling this screen is safe. A customer belonging to another merchant returns 404, not 403.
get.summary: A customer's verification status, checked with the provider

put.description: Sets or clears per-transaction, daily and monthly send ceilings for one of the merchant's own customers; manager-only. Amounts are decimal STRINGS in the customer's send currency, never JSON numbers. These limits ARE enforced, on the merchant payment path only - a payment that would breach one is refused with 422 LIMIT_EXCEEDED carrying the limit, the amount used, what remains and the period. Daily and monthly are calendar periods in UTC, and a payment awaiting payment or approval already counts against them. If a payment is later cancelled or rejected the headroom returns. A ceiling set in a different currency from the payment is refused rather than ignored. Omit a field or send an empty string to remove that ceiling; omit all three to remove limits entirely.

get.description: Notes this merchant's own staff have recorded about one of their customers, newest first. These are the merchant's notes only - Syka's internal administrative and compliance annotations on the same customer live elsewhere and are never returned here. Each note carries the author's name as it was when the note was written, so a note stays attributable after the staff member leaves.
get.summary: List staff notes on a customer

post.description: Records a note against one of the merchant's own customers, attributed to the authenticated staff member. Notes are append-only - there is no edit or delete - because they are a record of what staff observed at a point in time and an editable record is not a record. The note is visible to the merchant's own staff and to Syka administrators, and never to another merchant.
post.summary: Add a staff note to a customer

get.description: Payments this merchant has processed for one of its own customers, newest first, plus a rollup of counts and settled totals. Scoped to the merchant as well as the customer: if a customer was previously served by another merchant, those earlier payments belong to that merchant's history and are not returned here. Rollup money figures are USDC settled amounts, the only unit that can be added across corridors, and count only completed payments.
get.summary: A customer's payment history with this merchant

get.description: Headline figures for a merchant manager: today's and this month's payment volume and fee revenue, the number of payments waiting in the approval queue, customer and staff counts, and a per-branch summary. Manager-only — merchant staff receive 403. All figures are scoped to the caller's own merchant and are computed live, so they reflect the same data the reports endpoints return.

How far the caller's own organisation is through setting itself up, as a list of steps each with a `completed` flag and the endpoint that completes it. Every step is derived from live data rather than a stored progress flag, so deleting your last branch or your last staff member is reflected immediately. `completed` is computed over the REQUIRED steps only (organisation details, approval thresholds, first customer) while `percent` counts them all, so a single-location merchant with no branches is not stuck below 100% forever. `partner_status` and `can_transact` are separate and matter more than the checklist: a merchant can finish every step and still be unable to send payments if Syka has not activated the organisation, and `note` says so when that is the case.

Payments processed by the authenticated staff member's own merchant, newest first, filterable by status, type, currency, date range, branch, submitting staff member and customer. Use ?status=processing to watch payments in flight. Every id filter is validated against the caller's own merchant, so a branch, staff or customer id belonging to another merchant returns 404 rather than an empty page. Provider order identifiers are never included.

post.description: Submits a payment for one of the merchant's own customers and applies the merchant's risk rules, which is why the response is a union - always read the action field rather than assuming a 2xx means the money is moving. action=processed (201) means the payment was created and the response carries the customer's checkout URL. action=queued_for_approval (202) means it is waiting on a merchant manager and NO funds have been collected and no checkout exists yet. action=security_check_required (200) means the amount is at or above the merchant's re-authentication threshold: nothing was written, the staff member must confirm their password at /merchant/payments/security-check, and then resubmit this identical request with the returned security_token. An amount at or above the merchant's block threshold is refused outright with 422 AMOUNT_BLOCKED rather than being returned as an action. Blocked customers are refused, and a payment that would breach the customer's limits is refused with 422 LIMIT_EXCEEDED before any of the threshold routing runs. Requires an Idempotency-Key header.

Returns a locked exchange rate, the fee split and the total the customer will pay for a payment the merchant is about to submit. The quote is bound to the named customer as its sender, so it can only be spent on that customer's payment, and it expires within about 90 seconds. Both payment rails matter and are separate: send_payment_type is how the CUSTOMER funds the payment, while the beneficiary's payment code is how the RECIPIENT is paid - a quote priced on one funding rail can only be sent on that rail, because the fee and the rate both differ per rail.

Re-authenticates the signed-in staff member and returns a single-use security_token valid for five minutes, to be sent back on the payment that triggered the check. The token is bound to the specific staff member, customer and quote, so it cannot be reused on a different payment - and because a quote fixes the amount, currencies and recipient rail, that binding covers all of them. Rate limited: this endpoint verifies a password, so repeated attempts are throttled. A wrong password returns the same message regardless of why it failed.
post.summary: Confirm your password for a high-value payment

parameters.description: Password and the payment to authorise
parameters.name: request

get.description: Returns the ordered lifecycle timeline for one of the merchant's own payments, suitable for polling while it is in flight. Reading this also asks the payment provider for the order's true state when the payment is not yet finished and has not been checked in the last twenty seconds, so a payment whose provider notification was lost still advances for whoever is watching it. Reconciliation is best-effort: if the provider is unreachable the locally known state is returned rather than an error. A reference belonging to another merchant returns 404.

Returns a printable receipt for one of the merchant's own COMPLETED payments; a payment that has not settled yet is refused, because a receipt for money that has not arrived is a document a customer will act on wrongly. A reference belonging to another merchant returns 404.

The caller's own organisation record: legal and trading name, partner code, referral code, country, contacts, tier, status and the commission arrangement in force. Readable by all merchant staff. This is a NARROW projection of what Syka holds - internal scores, risk level, status history and relationship notes are deliberately not included. `referral_code` is what attributes a customer who signs up themselves to this merchant. `can_transact` is false whenever the organisation is suspended, terminated or still pending, and is the thing to check before showing a "send payment" button.

Side-by-side comparison of the merchant's branches: staff count, payments, completions, settled volume and fee contribution. Manager-only - merchant staff receive 403, because this exposes every branch's numbers to whoever runs it. A merchant with no branches configured sees a single "unattributed" row covering all its payments; branches are created by a Syka administrator.

Verification status across the merchant's customers, customers the merchant has blocked, and payments held or refused for risk reasons. Verification is performed by Syka's identity provider, so these are the statuses recorded on each customer rather than an assessment made here. Payments held for compliance review are held by SYKA, not by the merchant, and are released by Syka after review - approving them in the merchant queue will not release them.

post.description: Builds a report from a chosen set of metrics, groupings and filters. Every metric, grouping and filter name must come from the closed catalogue returned by GET /merchant/reports/templates - an unrecognised name is rejected with 400 rather than ignored, because silently dropping a filter WIDENS the query and returns more than was asked for. Filter values are validated by type: a status must be a real status, a currency a three-letter code, and a branch, staff or customer id must belong to the caller's own merchant or the request returns 404. At most 2 groupings and 6 metrics; the window may not exceed 366 days; results are capped at 5,000 rows and the response says so when the cap is reached. Set output_format to csv, xlsx or pdf to download the file instead of JSON.

Sets up a report to be generated and emailed daily, weekly or monthly to named recipients. Supply either a saved template_id or an inline config; when a template is used its definition is COPIED, so later edits to the template do not silently change what a schedule already approved delivers. Each run covers the period that has just CLOSED - a daily report delivered on the 5th covers the 4th - so a delivered figure never changes afterwards. Runs are claimed atomically, so running more than one server cannot deliver the same report twice, and a run that fails records the reason on the schedule and retries at its next boundary rather than every minute. If the mail transport cannot attach files the report is emailed as a summary rather than not at all.

get.description: One row per customer who transacted in the window: payment count, settled volume, first and last payment, and days since their last one. Customers with no payment in the window are not listed, so this is an activity report rather than a directory - use the customer list for that. The summary counts customers with no payment in the last 30 days as at risk; that threshold is a judgement, stated in the report rather than hidden in it.

Per-staff-member payment counts, completions, settled volume and fee contribution, ordered by volume. Pass staff_id (or staffId) to narrow to one person. Payments taken before staff attribution existed, or by an account since removed, are grouped as "unattributed" rather than dropped, so the rows still add up to the merchant total. A staff id belonging to another merchant returns 404.

Fee revenue over time, bucketed by day, week or month. The fee column is Syka's platform fee on the merchant's completed payments, in USDC - it is the base the merchant's commission is calculated from, not the commission itself, which is on the commission statement. Only completed payments count: a payment awaiting checkout has earned nothing. Filter by branch with ?branch= or ?branch_id=.

The merchant's own saved custom-report definitions and active schedules, plus the catalogue of metrics, groupings and filters a custom report may contain. The catalogue is generated from the same tables the server validates against, so a picker built from it cannot offer something the server will reject. It also carries the limits that apply: maximum groupings, maximum rows and the longest date range allowed.

post.description: Saves a custom-report definition under a name for reuse. The definition is validated against the metric, grouping and filter catalogue before it is stored, so an unrunnable template can never be saved and then fail every time somebody opens it. Template names are unique within a merchant; reusing one returns 409.

get.description: Payment volume and counts broken down by status, followed by a breakdown by destination currency in the same table (destination rows are prefixed "to "). Money columns are USDC settled amounts, which is the only unit that can be added across corridors; send volumes are listed per currency and never summed together, because adding GHS to NGN produces a number that means nothing. Settled and fee figures count only completed payments. Defaults to the current calendar month; the window may not exceed 366 days.

Payment counts and settled volume per period with the change against the previous period in the same table, so the first row has no change. Growth from zero is shown as "new" rather than as a percentage, because a first period of trading is not a percentage story. No forecast is produced: projecting from a single merchant's recent volume would be a guess presented as a figure, and a merchant would plan against it.

Downloads one of the fixed reports as a file. The type must be one of transaction-summary, customer-activity, performance, revenue, trend-analysis, branch-performance or compliance, and it honours the same filters as the equivalent JSON endpoint. Formats are csv (default), xlsx and pdf; PDF is capped at 5,000 rows, which is the same cap every merchant report already carries, and its built-in fonts cannot render non-Latin text. branch-performance remains manager-only in this form too.

The two roles a merchant account can hold, with a label, a description and the exact list of permissions each one carries. Use it to populate the role picker when inviting a team member. MERCHANT_STAFF registers and serves customers and submits their payments; MERCHANT_MANAGER does all of that plus deciding queued approvals, blocking customers, setting their limits and comparing branches. The list is generated from the same permission catalogue the server enforces with, so it cannot describe access the guards do not actually grant.

The risk thresholds in force for the caller's organisation, plus the range each one may be set within. Readable by all merchant staff, because these are what decide whether a given payment goes straight through, queues for a manager, asks for a security check, or is refused - a staff member whose payment queued deserves to see why. `configured` is false when nobody has ever set them, in which case the values shown are Syka's platform defaults rather than a choice somebody made. All amounts are decimal STRINGS in USDC and are compared against each payment's settled amount, which is the only unit every corridor shares; a threshold in local currency is not possible because nothing converts one at check time.

put.description: Sets the risk thresholds for the caller's own organisation. MANAGER-ONLY; merchant staff receive 403. Every field is optional - omit one to leave it unchanged. Amounts are decimal STRINGS in USDC. `approval_threshold` is the amount above which a payment waits for a manager's decision; `security_check_threshold` the amount above which the submitting staff member must re-enter their password; `block_threshold` the amount above which a payment is refused outright (422 AMOUNT_BLOCKED) and has no default, because refusing a payment is something a partner opts into. The block threshold must be HIGHER than the approval threshold - otherwise every payment that would have queued is refused before a manager can see it, and the request returns 422 INVALID_CONTROLS. A value above the platform maximum returns 422 CONTROL_ABOVE_PLATFORM_MAXIMUM naming the ceiling; the ranges are in `limits` on the GET. The organisation this applies to is taken from your session, never from the request, so these settings can only ever be your own.

422.description: Thresholds out of range or inconsistent

get.description: Returns the merchant's own staff accounts (MERCHANT_STAFF and MERCHANT_MANAGER), optionally narrowed to one branch with branch_id. Only identity, role, status and branch are returned — never credentials or two-factor state. A branch_id belonging to another merchant returns 404 rather than an empty list, so the endpoint cannot be used to probe for branch ids. Staff accounts are provisioned by a Syka administrator, not from this app.

post.description: Creates a login for one of the caller's own people - the merchant equivalent of a teller account - and returns a temporary password that is shown ONCE and is also emailed to them. MANAGER-ONLY; merchant staff receive 403. Set `manager: true` for MERCHANT_MANAGER, otherwise the account is MERCHANT_STAFF (see GET /merchant/roles). `branch_id` is optional but matters: it is copied onto every customer that person registers and every payment they take, and the branch reports are built from those snapshots, so a staff member without one produces unattributed rows. A branch id that is not yours returns 404. The employer is taken from your session, never from the request, so a team member can only ever be created inside your own organisation. The email address must not already exist on the platform (409).

Requires an Idempotency-Key header. post.description: Verifies the signed-in teller's own password and returns a SINGLE-USE token that authorises one specific send. Send it back as security_token on POST /teller/transactions/create. Why it exists: a teller workstation left unlocked at a counter is a physically accessible session, and without this the person who sits down at it can move a customer's money with nothing more than the open tab. The token is bound to (teller, customer, quote), so it cannot be replayed onto a different customer or a different price - and because a quote fixes the amount, both currencies and the recipient's rail, re-quoting invalidates the token by design. It is valid for 5 minutes and is consumed on first use, whether or not that use succeeds. A wrong password and an unknown account return the SAME 401, deliberately. RATE LIMITED to 3 attempts per 10 minutes per teller+IP, shared with every other OTP-class endpoint - without that this would be a password oracle against teller accounts.

post.description:
`send_payment_type` (the SENDER's funding rail — see POST /transactions/send) is REQUIRED and applies to the WHOLE batch: every child send is funded the same way.
Creates a batch of sends to saved beneficiaries (corporate accounts). The batch is returned immediately in status "processing" with every item "pending"; it is then processed asynchronously and each item becomes an independent child transaction with its own checkout URL. Poll GET /transactions/bulk/{reference} for progress (status processing → created|partial|failed). Requires an Idempotency-Key header. Per-item failures are reported in the batch without failing the whole request.

get.description: Returns an empty payment template with the exact column headers the upload endpoint expects — Bank Name, Account Number, Account Name, Amount, Description — plus two example rows. Defaults to XLSX; pass `?format=csv` for CSV. This is a FILE download, not the standard JSON envelope. Always start from this file: the parser matches columns by header name (case-, space- and punctuation-insensitive, so "account_number" and "ACCOUNT NO." also work) rather than by position, but the three required columns are Account Number, Account Name and Amount.

post.description: Accepts a multipart `file` (.xlsx or .csv, max 2 MB, max 200 payment rows) and parses it into rows. Nothing is sent and no money moves — this only parses. Returns an `upload_id` plus every parsed row with its 1-based spreadsheet row number so errors can be pointed at the right line. Fully blank rows are skipped (trailing empty spreadsheet rows are normal). NEXT STEP: POST /transactions/bulk/validate with the returned `upload_id`. Parsed rows are held for 24 HOURS and are scoped to the uploading user; after that you must upload again. Corporate accounts only.

Checks every parsed row and tries to resolve it to one of your saved beneficiaries by account number. Each row comes back as `matched` (linked to a `beneficiary_id`, ready to send), `unmatched` (valid but no saved beneficiary — `suggested_action: create_beneficiary`) or `invalid` (with a specific `error`). IMPORTANT — account names are ALWAYS reported as `name_verification: "unverified_name"`: confirming that a name belongs to an account requires a third-party bank account-name verification service, which is not connected, so we never claim a name was verified. Unmatched rows are NOT auto-created as beneficiaries — an unverified account number silently becoming a saved payee is a fraud vector; save them with POST /beneficiaries and call validate again. When every row is matched, submit with POST /transactions/bulk passing `upload_id`. Corporate accounts only.

get.description: Returns a bulk/payroll batch with each item's child transaction reference, status, and checkout URL.

post.description:
Prices a cross-border send: how much the recipient receives for a given send amount. Internally chains a payin quote (send fiat → USDC) and a payout quote (USDC → receive fiat). The returned quote_id is short-lived (≈90s) and is required by POST /transactions/send.
The stablecoin settlement leg is internal and invisible to the user; both send and receive amounts are fiat.
Pass `send_payment_type` (+ optional `send_payment_code`) — the SENDER's funding rail, from GET /config/payment-methods?direction=deposit&currency=<send_currency> — to price the payin leg on the rail actually charged. Doing so LOCKS the quote to that rail: POST /transactions/send inherits it, and sending on a different one returns 422 QUOTE_METHOD_MISMATCH.

get.description: Returns the authenticated user's scheduled/recurring payments and their next run time.

post.description:
Creates a scheduled or recurring send to a SAVED beneficiary. At each run the backend creates the transaction and notifies you with a fresh checkout link (the MVP is pass-through, so it can't auto-charge). Frequency is once|daily|weekly|monthly.
`send_payment_type` (the SENDER's funding rail — see POST /transactions/send) is REQUIRED, because nobody is present to choose one when a run fires. Schedules created before this field existed cannot run and must be cancelled and recreated.

delete.description: Cancels an active scheduled/recurring payment so no further runs occur.

post.description:
Initiates a remittance against a quote. Creates the transaction and a payin order, returning a checkout_url the SENDER must open to pay. The payout to the recipient is triggered automatically once the payin settles (via webhook). Requires KYC-approved status.
`send_payment_type` is REQUIRED: it is how the SENDER funds this transfer (their deposit rail), which is a different thing from `beneficiary.payment_type` (how the RECIPIENT is paid). Get the values from GET /config/payment-methods?direction=deposit&currency=<send_currency> — `type` → `send_payment_type`, `code` → `send_payment_code`. The payment provider rejects a collection order without it. You may omit both if the quote was already created with them.
Requires the Idempotency-Key header (UUID). A replay with the same key returns the original transaction without creating a new one — EXCEPT when the earlier attempt failed before any payment order existed (no funds were collected), in which case the retry creates a fresh attempt instead of returning the dead transaction.
Optional `success_redirect_url` / `failure_redirect_url` control where the provider returns the sender's browser after the hosted checkout — pass your own (e.g. http://localhost:3000/payment/complete in development, or a mobile deep link) instead of the server default. They must point at an origin in this deployment's ALLOWED_ORIGINS list, otherwise the request is rejected with 400 INVALID_REDIRECT_URL: an unvalidated post-payment redirect would be a phishing hand-off. The values are snapshotted onto the transaction, so a held transfer resumes to the same destination.

parameters.description: Unique key to make this send idempotent (UUID)
parameters.name: Idempotency-Key

get.description: Returns one transaction (by reference) owned by the authenticated user. If the transfer is still in flight, this endpoint ASKS THE PROVIDER for its true state before responding and applies whatever it reports, so a status advances even when the completion webhook never arrived — which is always the case against a local development server the provider cannot reach. The check is throttled to roughly once every 20 seconds per transaction and is best-effort: an unreachable provider returns the last known state rather than an error.

post.description: Cancels a transfer the sender hasn't paid for yet (status INITIATED or PENDING). No funds have been collected, so no ledger entries are posted. Completed/processing transfers cannot be cancelled.

get.description: Returns the receipt for a COMPLETED transaction the user owns. Defaults to the structured JSON fields so the client can render its own layout. Pass `?format=pdf` to get a ready-made branded PDF instead — that response is a FILE download (Content-Disposition attachment), not the standard JSON envelope, so do not try to parse it as JSON. NOTE: the PDF uses Latin-1 core fonts; characters outside that range (e.g. non-Latin scripts in a recipient name) render as "?" until a Unicode font is embedded.

post.description: Drives one leg of YOUR OWN transfer to a provider order status, WAITS for the provider to apply it, reads the result back through the normal webhook path, and returns the transfer plus a simulation block saying what happened and what to do next. Sandbox only - in production the payment partner refuses the call and nothing changes, because this endpoint never sets a status itself. A REMITTANCE HAS TWO LEGS and completing one takes two calls: {"status":"fund_settled"} settles the PAYIN (the customer's money), which moves the transfer to PROCESSING and creates the payout; then {"leg":"payout","status":"fund_settled"} settles the PAYOUT, which completes it. simulation.next_step names the next call. The provider applies a simulation asynchronously (it reports fund_processing first); this endpoint polls for up to about 12 seconds and returns 200 with simulation.applied=true once the provider has reached the status, or 202 with applied=false if it is still applying - then poll GET /transactions/{reference} rather than simulating again. A retry is safe either way: if the order is already at the requested status the provider is not asked again. If the payin settled but the payout could not be created (for example the provider refused the recipient's details), the transfer is ON_HOLD and this returns 422 PAYOUT_NOT_CREATED with the reason - an administrator releases it with POST /admin/transactions/{reference}/release once the details are fixed. A leg the provider has already finished returns 422 LEG_ALREADY_TERMINAL naming the provider's status. The provider validates the status PER ORDER TYPE: a payin accepts fund_settled, fund_failed, expired and manual_review; asset_* is refused on a payin with 400 SIMULATION_STATUS_UNSUPPORTED; an illegal transition returns 422 SIMULATION_TRANSITION_REFUSED. error_code is passed through so a specific failure can be reproduced. A transfer you did not send (or process as the teller) returns 404, never 403.
post.summary: Simulate a transfer's provider status (SANDBOX ONLY)

404.description: Not your transfer, or no such leg

422.description: No leg available to simulate, leg already terminal, or payout not created

get.description: Returns an ordered lifecycle timeline (created → collection → payout → completed/failed) for a transaction the user owns. Use it for the tracking screen. Like GET /transactions/{reference}, an in-flight transfer is reconciled against the provider before responding (throttled, best-effort), so the timeline advances even when the completion webhook never reached this host.

post.description: Confirms the 6-digit code sent by POST /users/me/email/verify and marks the account's email as verified — `email_verified` on GET /users/me flips to true. Returns 400 INVALID_OTP when the code is wrong or expired (request a new one), or 422 EMAIL_ALREADY_VERIFIED if it was already confirmed. Shares the same OTP rate-limit bucket as the send step.

Emails a 6-digit verification code to the signed-in user's address, valid for 15 minutes. Also serves as the RESEND path — call it again for a new code (the previous one is invalidated). Returns the masked address so the UI can show where the code went; outside production the response also carries `dev_otp` so the code can be read without a mailbox. Only the fields sent are changed. `first_name` / `last_name` may be sent to CORRECT the name given at registration, but only while it is still ours alone: refused with 422 `IDENTITY_LOCKED` once identity verification is approved or under review, and with 422 `NAME_HELD_BY_PROVIDER` once the user has been registered with the payment provider (the provider's record cannot be updated, so the two would disagree) - in both cases the user must contact support. Re-sending the stored name unchanged is never refused. Names must match the provider's rule: letters from any alphabet (accents included), spaces, hyphens, apostrophes and full stops - no digits or other symbols (400 otherwise). A name refused by the provider at verification time is reported as 422 `NAME_NOT_ACCEPTED` by the KYC initiate endpoints, naming the field to correct here.

post.description:
Server-to-server endpoint called by TransFi, NOT by frontend apps. Frontend developers do not need to call this — it is invoked automatically by TransFi's infrastructure when payment or KYC events occur.
Security: every request must include a valid HMAC-SHA256 signature in the X-Transfi-Hmac-Hash header (hex digest over the raw request body, keyed with the shared webhook secret). Requests without a valid signature are rejected with 401.
Every event is recorded for audit and de-duplicated by eventId (TransFi retries up to 8×/2h). Already-processed events are acknowledged with 200 without reprocessing; a processing failure returns a non-2xx so TransFi retries delivery.
Events handled — User: kyc_success, kyc_failed, kyc_manual_review, kyc_rejected, kyb_success, user_approved, user_rejected. Orders: fund_settled, fund_failed, fund_scheduled, asset_settled, manual_review, expired.

parameters.description: HMAC-SHA256 hex signature of the raw request body
parameters.name: X-Transfi-Hmac-Hash

sections_failed.description:
SectionsFailed lists sections that errored or timed out. Their arrays are
empty, which is NOT the same as "nothing matched" — surface it in the UI.

sections_omitted.description: SectionsOmitted lists sections the caller's role is not allowed to see.

is_cost.description:
IsCost marks a line that REDUCES net revenue. Rendering it as income
would overstate the business by the provider's take.

required.description:
Required is true until a compliance officer clears it. While true the
person cannot send money.

approved_tier.description:
ApprovedTier and ApprovedCommission are the commercial terms the approver
agreed, carried into the partner record by Onboard.

ApproveApplication has written both to Mongo since the pipeline was built,
but there were no fields here to decode them back and Onboard never read
them — so the tier and rate an approver set were silently discarded and
every onboarded partner started on the platform default. Latent while
admins created partners directly; self-registration makes onboarding the
normal path, which is what surfaced it.

reference.description:
Reference is the human-readable handle an applicant quotes to support
("MA-7F3A91C4"). Distinct from TrackingToken, which is a credential.

source.description:
Source distinguishes an application filed on the public site from one an
admin keyed in, which is what a reviewer needs to know about its provenance:
nothing about a self-registration has been verified by us.

target_audience.description: TargetAudience is who the applicant serves, collected on the public form.

approval_max_age_hours.description:
ApprovalMaxAgeHours is how long a queued payment may wait before the INTENT
is treated as stale and the payment must be submitted again.

It used to bound the RATE as well — the quote was honoured as-is, so an old
approval meant an old price. Approving now re-prices at the live rate, so
this bounds only how long a customer's instruction stays live. A customer
who walked into a branch a week ago has moved on whatever the rate is doing.

Hours rather than a time.Duration: a Duration is nanoseconds on the wire
and in the stored document, which is not a number anyone can read or type
into a config screen.

requote_tolerance_bps.description:
RequoteToleranceBps is how far a re-priced payment may move, in basis
points, before approving it requires an explicit acceptance of the new
figures. Applies to whichever side of the transfer actually moved.

configured.description:
Configured is false when nobody has ever set these, so a UI can say
"platform defaults" rather than implying somebody chose them.

branch_id.description:
BranchID is what makes a branch more than a label: it is copied onto every
customer this person registers and every payment they take, which is what
the branch reports are built from. Optional — a merchant with no branches
is legitimate, and their rows simply report as unattributed.

manager.description:
Manager grants MERCHANT_MANAGER instead of MERCHANT_STAFF: the difference
is deciding payment approvals, blocking customers, setting their limits and
comparing branches.

application_id.description:
ApplicationID is set on a document uploaded during self-registration,
before any partner exists. Onboarding re-stamps PartnerID onto these
(AttachDocumentsToPartner) and leaves this in place, so the provenance of
a due-diligence file survives.

channel_partner_id.description:
PartnerID is zero until the application it came from is onboarded. It is
omitempty so an application-stage document carries no partner key at all
rather than a NilObjectID, which would match a partner-scoped query for
another zero value.

url.description: URL is a short-lived presigned download link, populated on read only.

hint.description: Hint is the explanatory line under the label on the upload card.

channel.description: Channel defaults to email. SMS requires a contact phone.

check_in_days.description: CheckInDays schedules the first relationship call. Defaults to 30.

manager_first_name.description:
ManagerFirstName/LastName/Email/Phone identify the person who receives the
manager login. Defaults to the application's primary contact.

tier.description:
Tier and Commission override the terms recorded at approval. Both are
OPTIONAL: left out, the application's approved_tier / approved_commission
are used, which is the normal path. They exist so a last-minute correction
does not require re-approving.

controls.description:
Controls are the merchant-path risk thresholds. Read them through
EffectiveControls(), never directly.

controls_set_at.description:
ControlsSetAt is when a human last chose these thresholds.

Needed because Controls has no "unset" state a reader can see:
EffectiveControls fills every blank with a platform default, by design, so
a partner nobody has configured is indistinguishable from one deliberately
set to the defaults. The onboarding checklist has to tell those apart, and
a settings screen should not claim somebody chose a value they did not.

manager_user_id.description: ManagerUserID is the merchant-context account provisioned at onboarding.

referral_code.description:
ReferralCode attributes a customer to this partner at registration. Unique
and sparse — a partner without one simply cannot be self-attributed.

decision_note.description:
DecisionNote is the rejection reason, once there is one. Approval detail
(tier, commission) is deliberately absent: those are commercial terms
discussed with the partner, not a status page field.

active.description:
Active false closes a branch: it stops appearing in the merchant's
pickers, but every customer and payment already attributed to it keeps
that attribution, so historical branch reports do not change.

kind.description:
Kind mirrors the partner's kind so the payouts list can be filtered by
merchant vs partner without a join.

max_volume.description: MaxVolume of "" or "0" means unbounded (the top bracket).

fields.description:
Fields is the TYPED schema for RequiredFields. Use it to build the beneficiary
form AND to send payout_details with the right JSON types — some corridors
need non-string values (e.g. US-ACH bankAddress is an object and invoiceIds is
an array). A form that submits everything as a string will be rejected by the
provider with an invalid_type error.

pattern.description:
Format rules, when the provider sets them. A value that breaks one is
refused at beneficiary save and at send — before any money moves — rather
than by the provider when the payout is created after the customer paid.

amount.description:
Amount is the unit price as a decimal STRING, never a number: a float64
cannot represent money exactly and JSON has only float64.

due_date.description: DueDate is YYYY-MM-DD. Without one an invoice is never overdue.

min_qty.description: MinQty/MaxQty bound how many units may be paid for. Both default to 1.

payout_rail.description:
PayoutRail is how the ISSUER wants to be paid. Optional: without it the
invoice is a register entry settled with mark-paid, which is what it was

quantity.description:
Quantity is how many units to pay for, within the invoice's min/max.
Defaults to min_qty.

send_currency.description: SendCurrency is what the payer pays in. Defaults to the invoice currency.

send_payment_type.description:
SendPaymentType / SendPaymentCode are how the PAYER funds it — their own
deposit rail, from
GET /config/payment-methods?direction=deposit&currency=<your currency>.
Required for the same reason POST /transactions/send requires it: the
provider refuses a collection order without one.

account_name.description:
AccountName is who the invoice is FOR, as the issuer typed it. Free text
on purpose: an invoice is frequently raised against somebody who has no
Syka account, and requiring one would make the register useless for
exactly the customers it is meant to track.

unit price; MinQty/MaxQty bound how many units may be paid for.

paid_at.description:

reference when it was paid through Syka, and empty when the issuer
recorded an outside payment -- the two are deliberately distinguishable,
because one is verifiable and the other is the issuer's word.

payable.description:
Payable is false when the issuer has not said how they want to be paid, or
the invoice is already settled or withdrawn.

payment_label.description:

"mtn (local_wallet), Ghana". Enough for the payer to recognise it; not
enough to be the issuer's account details.

the API is reached on different hosts per environment and the server has no
reliable way to know which one the caller came through.

Email / Phone are the provider's raw statuses, e.g. "verified" or

email_at.description:
EmailAt / PhoneAt are when each was last initiated or completed. The
verification link is valid for ten minutes from that moment, so an old
timestamp on an "initiated" status means it has long expired.

note.description:
Note is user-facing guidance, present only when Verified is false. Show it
verbatim; it is the whole point of this block.

verified.description:
Verified reports whether the provider is satisfied. EITHER channel is
enough — that is the provider's own rule.

resumed.description:
Resumed is true when verify_url is an EXISTING unfinished session rather
than a newly created one — the user closed the hosted flow and is being
returned to the same link. No new provider session was created.

can_retry.description:
CanRetry reports whether starting a new verification is allowed right
now. False while a human review is pending or after a final decline.

contact_verification.description:
ContactVerification is the provider's SEPARATE email/phone check, which
blocks verification and transfers until one of the two is satisfied.

It exists because users hit a wall nobody could explain: the provider
emails them a link, it expires in ten minutes, and until now the app said

provider_status.description:
ProviderStatus is the verification provider's own state, populated when
we reconciled against them on this call. Diagnostic — drive UI off
kyc_status, not this.

reject_reasons.description:
RejectReasons explain a failure so the user knows what to fix
(e.g. BAD_SELFIE, AGE_REQUIREMENT_MISMATCH).

ResumeURL is the still-valid hosted-verification link when a session was
started but not finished. Present so the app can offer "continue
verification" instead of leaving the user on a dead-end status screen.

at submission and is NOT re-quoted on release, so an old approval would
honour an old rate at our expense.

requoted_at.description:
Re-quote audit. A payment approved after a wait is released at TODAY's
price, not the one it was submitted at, and the manager may have had to
accept a materially different figure — so what was originally quoted, and
how many times it was re-priced, has to survive on the record.

settle_amount.description:

WAS. Reading the partner's current threshold at decision time would make a
past approval look wrong the moment an administrator retunes the partner.

blocked_by.description:
BlockedBy names gates OTHER than this approval that are still holding the
payment. Without it, a manager approves a doubly-gated payment, sees the
status stay ON_HOLD, and reasonably concludes the button is broken.

Stale reports that the payment has waited longer than the merchant's
approval window, so approving will be refused and it must be submitted
again.

It is about the INTENT, not the price: approving re-prices at the live rate,
so an old payment is not mispriced — but a customer who walked in a week
ago has moved on, and nobody should release their instruction now without
asking them again.

moved_percent.description:
MovedPercent is the larger of the two moves that matter — what the sender
pays and what the recipient gets — as a plain decimal string.

declaration_accepted.description:
DeclarationAccepted must be true. A registration is a set of statements
made by the person registering it; recording that they were made is the
point.

business.description:
Corporate — required when customer_type is "corporate", forbidden otherwise.
Directors and UBOs each need at least one entry: no KYB provider can verify
a company with none named.

customer_type.description:
CustomerType is "individual" or "corporate". Defaults to "corporate", which
is what this endpoint did before individuals were supported — so every
caller written against the original business-only contract keeps working
with no change at all.

individual.description: Individual — required when customer_type is "individual", forbidden otherwise.

redirect_url.description:
RedirectURL is where the customer's browser lands after they finish at the
verification provider. Optional; must be on an ALLOWED_ORIGINS origin.

Without it every merchant-registered customer was returned to the Syka
CONSUMER app, which is not where a merchant's customer came from and, for a
walk-in, not an app they have.

registered_address.description:
Shared. For an individual, registered_address is their RESIDENTIAL address —
the same key rather than a second field, because it plays the same role: it
is the address the payment provider verifies them at.

start_kyb.description:
StartKYB is the corporate-era name for StartVerification, still accepted so
existing callers keep working. StartVerification wins when both are sent.

start_verification.description:
StartVerification defaults to true. Set false to register the customer
without immediately opening a verification session — useful when the
paperwork is still being gathered.

manager.description:
Manager grants MERCHANT_MANAGER: deciding approvals, blocking customers,
setting their limits and comparing branches.

kyb.description:
KYB is set for a corporate customer and KYC for an individual — exactly one
of the two, never both. They carry the same shape; the separate keys exist
so a client can tell at a glance which kind of record it is looking at.

warnings.description:
Warnings names the non-fatal steps that did not complete. A director that
failed to save is fixable afterwards; losing the temporary password is not,
which is why those failures are reported rather than rolled back.

identity_locked.description:
IdentityLocked: the customer is verified, so LockedFields refuse changes
(422 IDENTITY_LOCKED). A correction goes to Syka support.

kyb.description:
KYB is set for a corporate customer and KYC for an individual — exactly
one of the two. Same shape; the separate keys let a client tell which kind
of record it is looking at without inspecting account_type.

limit_status.description:
LimitStatus reports the same ceilings with live consumption, and whether
they are actually being enforced. Enforced is real here, unlike the
platform tier limits which report enforced:false — a merchant needs to
know which of the two numbers on their screen will stop a payment.

url.description: URL is populated on read with a short-lived presigned link. Never stored.

can_retry.description:
CanRetry reports whether verification may be started again right now.
False during a human review and after a final decline.

contact_verification.description:
ContactVerification is the payment provider's OWN email/phone check, which
is separate from the Syka verification the customer completed at
registration and blocks transfers until one channel is satisfied. The
provider emails the customer a link valid for ten minutes; when this says
"initiated" with an old timestamp, that link was sent and never opened.

detail.description:
Detail names the blocker when Status is blocked_provider_registration:
the customer exists in our records but was never registered with the
payment provider, so verification cannot start and they can never transact.

resume_url.description:
ResumeURL is the customer's still-valid hosted-verification link when a
session was started and not finished. Hand it back to them rather than
starting a new one.

accept_quote_id.description:
AcceptQuoteID accepts a re-price the manager was shown.

Approving re-prices the payment at the live rate. When the figures move
more than the merchant's tolerance, the first call returns them for the
manager to look at rather than releasing silently; the second call carries
the quote id from that response. Within tolerance it is not needed.

notes.description:
Notes is optional on approve and REQUIRED on reject: a refusal the
submitting staff member cannot explain to the customer standing in front of
them is not a usable decision.

level.description: Level is the KYC tier to request (1-4). Defaults to 1.

redirect_url.description:
RedirectURL is where the customer lands after finishing at the provider.
Must be on an allow-listed origin. When omitted the server default is used.

commission.description:
Commission is the arrangement in force. A partner is entitled to know what
they earn; the accrual records behind it are at /merchant/... reports.

partner_status.description:
Status is the partner's own standing. A merchant can complete every step
and still be unable to transact if their partner record is not active, and
that is the first thing a stuck manager needs to see.

required.description:
Required steps decide `completed`. The optional ones still count towards
`percent`, so progress keeps moving without a one-person merchant with no
branches being told forever that they are not set up.

security_token.description:
SecurityToken is required only when a previous attempt returned
security_check_required. It is single-use and bound to this exact payment.

send_payment_type.description:
SendPaymentType is how the SENDER funds this transfer (their deposit rail) —
distinct from beneficiary.payment_type, which is how the RECIPIENT is paid.
The payment provider rejects a payin without it. Take the values from
GET /config/payment-methods?direction=deposit&currency=<send_currency>:
`type` → send_payment_type, `code` → send_payment_code.

success_redirect_url.description:
SuccessRedirectURL / FailureRedirectURL are where the provider returns the
sender's browser after they finish or abandon the hosted checkout. Optional
— when omitted the server-configured defaults apply. Must point at an
origin in this deployment's ALLOWED_ORIGINS list, otherwise the request is
rejected with 400 INVALID_REDIRECT_URL: an unvalidated post-payment
redirect would be a phishing hand-off.

thresholds.description:
Thresholds echoes what the decision was made against, so a UI can explain
"this needs approval because it is over X" without a second call.

receive_payment_code.description: Optional: the recipient payout rail, refines the payout-leg rate.

send_amount.description:
Provide EXACTLY ONE of send_amount (price by what the sender pays) or
receive_amount (price so the recipient receives exactly this).

send_payment_code.description:
Optional: the SENDER's funding rail (how they will pay for this transfer).
Fetch it from GET /config/payment-methods?direction=deposit&currency=<send_currency>.
Supplying it here prices the payin leg on the rail actually charged and locks
it onto the quote, so POST /transactions/send inherits it. The rail is
REQUIRED at send time, so pass it here whenever the user has already chosen.

definition.description:
Definition is COPIED from the template at scheduling time, not referenced.
A schedule that silently changed shape because somebody edited a template
would deliver a different report from the one that was approved.

customer_id.description:
The payment the token will authorise. The issued token is bound to these
values, so it cannot be replayed onto a different payment.

catalogue.description:
Catalogue ships the labels and descriptions so the UI never hardcodes
them and a new alert type appears without a client release.

threshold_usd.description:
ThresholdUSD only applies to amount-gated alerts. A decimal STRING, never
a float — money never touches float64 in this codebase.

resource_type.description:
ResourceType, ResourceRef and Action say what this notification is ABOUT,
so tapping it can open the thing rather than just marking it read.

A RESOURCE REFERENCE, deliberately, not a URL. Three different apps consume
this feed (user, teller, merchant) and the server does not know any of their
routing tables; a URL built here would be wrong for at least two of them and
would rot the moment one changed its paths. The client maps
{resource_type, action} to its own screen and uses resource_ref as the
argument -- and resource_ref is the same reference the rest of the API
already uses, e.g. "TX-9BDADD6ED0C3407388".

Empty on notifications created before 2026-09-12, and on broadcasts, which
are about nothing in particular. Clients must handle absence.

format.description: Format is csv (default), xlsx or pdf.

amount.description:
Amount + amount_type is the current contract: amount_type "send" (cash the
customer hands over, in send_currency) or "receive" (what the recipient
receives, in receive_currency). amount_received is a DEPRECATED alias always
treated as a SEND amount. Provide either amount or amount_received.

counter_payment_method.description: CounterPaymentMethod is how the customer settled AT THE COUNTER.

quote_id.description:
QuoteID is the quote returned by POST /teller/quote. Send it and the
customer is charged exactly the price the teller read to them; omit it and
the corridor is re-priced at send, which is the old behaviour and can
differ from what was quoted.

security_token.description:
SecurityToken is the single-use token from POST /teller/transactions/step-up.
Required only when the office requires a step-up for this send.

dob.description:
Optional at creation, but REQUIRED before the customer can be KYC-verified
(the financial partner needs date of birth + a residential address).

editable.description:
Editable says whether this teller app may change the record. False for a
customer who registered themselves or through a merchant: they own their
own details. Returned so the app can hide the edit form rather than let a
teller fill it in and discover a 403 on submit.

identity_locked.description:
IdentityLocked: the customer's identity is verified, so LockedFields refuse
changes even when Editable is true — contact details and the address can
still be edited, the legal name and date of birth cannot.

currency.description:
Cash reconciliation (decimal strings, in the shift Currency). The drawer
only grows during a shift: sends collect cash but pay the recipient from our
TransFi float, so cash is never removed by a send.

customer_user_id.description:
The payment the token will authorise. The token is bound to these values,
so it cannot be replayed onto a different customer or a different price.

staff.description: Staff counts. OpenShifts is who is at a counter right now.

transfers.description: Transfers this office keyed in, over the requested period.

rank.description:

Members with no transfers in the period share the last positions.

phone.description: E.164 or local when country_code set

redirect_url.description:
Optional: where the customer is redirected after completing KYC. When
omitted the server-configured default (TRANSFI_KYC_REDIRECT_URL) is used.

Category is the spending bucket derived from PurposeCode. See
financial.CategoryForPurposeCode — one mapping, shared with
GET /config/purpose-codes.

with the teller (cash | direct_debit | collected). A separate field from
the two above because a teller send has no provider funding rail at all.

direction.description:
Direction is "debit" (value leaving the viewer) or "credit" (value
arriving), derived at read time relative to the viewer — never stored.

the recipient is an encrypted snapshot, not a Syka user. So today only
ONRAMP is a credit and everything else is a debit. Do not build a
money-in-vs-money-out view on this until inbound remittances to Syka
users are modelled.

fee.description:
Fee is our platform fee in the send currency; TotalCost is what the
sender actually paid. Both were previously only on the quote, which meant
a history row could not show what a transfer cost.

rate.description:
Rate is receive-per-send, for display. It was stored on every transaction
and returned on the QUOTE and the RECEIPT but not here, so a history screen
had to derive it by dividing the amounts -- which is wrong, because the
amounts are net of fees and the quotient is not the rate the customer got.

recipient.description:
Recipient is where the money went: the masked account identifier and the
institution. Requested by the frontend on 2026-09-10 -- the detail screen
could name the person but not the account, which is the half a user checks
when they think they sent to the wrong place.

recipient_notification.description:
RecipientNotification says whether we were able to tell the recipient that
the money arrived, and if not, why.

The recipient is NOT a Syka user — the money lands in their mobile money or
bank account and the transfer appears in no app of theirs — so this message
is the only contact they get. Absent until the payout settles. `skipped`
with "no contact on file for this recipient" is normal for a payout rail
that carries no phone or email, and is not a failure of the transfer.

How the SENDER paid: their funding rail, not the recipient's payout rail.
Stored since the 2026-08-27 rail work and never serialised.

says the settle figure is USDC -- the value was knowable (it is a constant)
but unstated, and an amount without its currency is the one shape a money
API must not ship.

SendPaymentType is how the SENDER funds the whole batch (their deposit rail);
see SendRequest. Batch-level: every child send uses it.

Never the full identifier.

institution.description: Institution is the bank, mobile-money operator or wallet the money went to.

name.description: Name is the beneficiary as we recorded them.

payment_code.description: PaymentCode and PaymentType are the recipient's payout rail.

RecipientNotification says whether we were able to tell the recipient that
the money arrived, and if not, why.

The recipient is NOT a Syka user — the money lands in their mobile money or
bank account and the transfer appears in no app of theirs — so this message
is the only contact they get. Absent until the payout settles. `skipped`
with "no contact on file for this recipient" is normal for a payout rail
that carries no phone or email, and is not a failure of the transfer.

applied.description:
Applied is true when the provider reached the requested status within the
wait. False means it accepted the request and is still applying it: poll
GET /transactions/{reference} rather than sending the simulation again.

provider_status.description: ProviderStatus is the order's status at the provider when we stopped waiting.

category.description:
Category is the spending bucket derived from PurposeCode. See
financial.CategoryForPurposeCode — one mapping, shared with
GET /config/purpose-codes.

counter_payment_method.description:
CounterPaymentMethod is set on TELLER_SEND only: how the customer settled
with the teller (cash | direct_debit | collected). A separate field from
the two above because a teller send has no provider funding rail at all.

direction.description:
Direction is "debit" (value leaving the viewer) or "credit" (value
arriving), derived at read time relative to the viewer — never stored.

LIMITATION: a transaction has exactly one user-linked party (sender_id);
the recipient is an encrypted snapshot, not a Syka user. So today only
ONRAMP is a credit and everything else is a debit. Do not build a
money-in-vs-money-out view on this until inbound remittances to Syka
users are modelled.

fee.description:
Fee is our platform fee in the send currency; TotalCost is what the
sender actually paid. Both were previously only on the quote, which meant
a history row could not show what a transfer cost.

rate.description:
Rate is receive-per-send, for display. It was stored on every transaction
and returned on the QUOTE and the RECEIPT but not here, so a history screen
had to derive it by dividing the amounts -- which is wrong, because the
amounts are net of fees and the quotient is not the rate the customer got.

recipient.description:
Recipient is where the money went: the masked account identifier and the
institution. Requested by the frontend on 2026-09-10 -- the detail screen
could name the person but not the account, which is the half a user checks
when they think they sent to the wrong place.

country_code.description: ISO-3166-1 alpha-2; parses phone + sets user country

id_type.description:
Document identity (individuals). Before 2026-09-19 an administrator could
not change these at all — so once self-service editing was locked after
verification, a verified person with a renewed passport would have had no
route to correct their record.

phone.description: E.164 (e.g. +233…) or local when country_code is set

reason.description:
Reason is REQUIRED whenever an identity field actually changes — name, date
of birth, gender, country, any document field, or a company's registered
identity. It is written to the immutable change record. Contact and address
edits need none.

risk_level.description:
RiskLevel drives the default review cadence when next_scheduled_date is
omitted. Optional; falls back to MEDIUM.

permissions.description:
Permissions overrides the role's default permission set. Advisory only —
nothing evaluates it at request time yet.

role.description:
Role defaults to TELLER. TELLER_SUPERVISOR is a teller-context role that
currently carries the SAME permissions as TELLER — it is a reporting label
until supervisor-only behaviour exists.

first_name.description:
Names live on the user record, not the profile, and are correctable here
only until they reach the payment provider — see selfNameChange.

identity_locked.description:
IdentityLocked is true once the identity was verified (or while it is under
review at the provider). The fields in LockedFields then refuse changes with
422 IDENTITY_LOCKED — grey them out rather than letting the user try.

identity_review.description:
IdentityReview is present when an administrator has changed a verified
identity. While review.required is true the person cannot send money.

office.description:
Office is the branch a STAFF member is assigned to, resolved to a name and
code rather than left as a bare id. Present only for teller accounts;
customers have no office.

office_id was writable at teller creation and through assign-teller but was
never readable back, so there was no way to confirm an assignment had
worked or to show a teller's branch on their record.
